meaning_fixes.reason: Source 私はあっちへ！ is Ray declaring her own tactical movement ('I'll go that way!'), not calling out a spotted location. 'Over there!' reads as pointing something out rather than announcing her own maneuver, which drops the first-person sense of the line. 'Going there!' restores it and fits the 12-char budget (min(72, 2*7-2)).

checked_decisions.finding: Confirmed in work/glossary/character_names_021.json: Ray Beams (resource 2823071) is gender female per the wiki infobox despite the masculine-looking English name; this is an already-researched glossary fact, not an invented one. Feminine register kept via word choice, no pronoun invented for the speaker herself. Correct.

人の援護ばかり期待しないの literally 'don't only expect people's/others' support'; target 'Don't rely on my cover' narrows this to the speaker specifically. Plausible as a support pilot's own admonishment to a reckless ally (a common team-banter pattern in this corpus); not clearly wrong, left as phrasing choice.

敵もやるわね ('the enemy's good too') compressed to 'Impressive.' and 余裕がなくなってきたわね ('losing composure/margin') rendered as 'Running out of room.' Both drop or shift a noun (enemy; composure vs. space) under tight budgets but keep the same reaction/complaint sense; not reversals.

Extreme budget (6 visible chars, from 4 source chars 新手ね！) forces 'New!' for what literally means 'a new one/reinforcement, huh!'; already disclosed by the translator, confirmed unavoidable at this budget.

みんな逃げ足だけは一人前ね carries a mocking edge ('quite the professional -- at running away') that 'You're all fast runners' softens into a near-compliment. The softer tone is not inconsistent with Ray's kind/caring personality profile and does not reverse the underlying observation (enemies fleeing); left as phrasing choice.
